angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 316,544 km at 75.38 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 13.2668 +/- 0.0168 mas (same row, RUWE 1.13): 75.38 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.455 +/- 0.022 solar radii from Wells et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-133 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.487.1865W/abstract): 316,544 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.461 +/- 0.011 solar masses from Wells et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-133 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.487.1865W/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3655 +/- 80 K from Wells et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-133 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.487.1865W/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Wells et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-133 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.487.1865W/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-133.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.786, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
